title: A walk never takes the keyboard, the pointer or focus from the person
goal: User 2026-09-26: 'when you test, you're completely stealing my computer. I can't even type... Just to say stop testing I had to pull focus back to the window at least 5 times.' The intake window added a stopgap (walks wait for the person to step away and stop when they return: queue/bin/person-at-mac.sh, exit 6 DEFERRED), which means walks rarely run while the user works. Find what actually steals input and remove it, so walks are harmless whenever they run. Leading theory, UNPROVEN: walks that open real menus call NSMenu.popUp (PlaytestHarness.swift:8565 and :8761), whose tracking loop takes every key press system-wide until it closes; also orderFrontRegardless on guide and capture windows (PlaytestHarness.swift:367, CaptureDiag.swift:308), NSApp.activate in ShortcutDiag.swift:48, and each launch of the probe. Test only while the Mac is idle (the gate does this) and measure, never assume.
notes: Filed from the intake window. Stopgap landed the same day in probe-app.sh, playtest.sh, playtest-all.sh, sweep.sh.
acceptance: A measurement harness logs, every 100 ms while a walk runs, the frontmost app, the key window's owner, and whether a keystroke typed into a TextEdit window in front lands there (synthesised into TextEdit by pid, not through the HID tap); run over the whole walk set in the night window, it names every walk and step that takes focus or eats a key

Every cause found is removed: menus are driven by invoking the item's action (or a harness menu model) instead of a real popUp tracking loop, windows are ordered without activation or raising above other apps, the probe runs as an accessory app that never becomes active during walks
After the fix the same harness shows zero focus changes and zero lost keystrokes across the whole set
Then the idle gate is relaxed: walks may run while the person is present, and only the full sweep keeps its idle requirement (write the change in person-at-mac.sh, probe-app.sh and CLAUDE.md)
A drill in queue/bin proves it and runs in the rotating check

log.note: owns these walks: a-clip-s-sound-is-linked-under-it-walk, effects-remembered-walk, locked-layer-key-press-walk, tutorial-a-title-that-moves-walk

Measured first: built queue/bin/focus-canary.swift + focus-drill.sh. The canary is a full-screen stand-in window holding the front; every 100ms it logs front app, key window, probe windows above it and probe menus. A synthesized key cannot measure routing (a key posted to own queue or by pid landed 39/39 with Finder in front), so 'landed' reads the routing itself: canary active + key + no probe menu. Deviation from acceptance item 1, explained in the canary's header.

Causes found, each tied to a walk and step: (1) opening a recording ran AppCoordinator.openWindow -> NSApp.activate, making the probe the active app. (2) the guide check orderFrontRegardless'd the window at every step. (3) rightClick and panelMenu popped a real menu (tracking loop takes every key) even with no picture asked; SwiftUI Menu (Add Effect) only fills rows in popUpButtonCell:willShowMenu:. (4) a press's release lifts the walk window to the front inside AppKit (a hook on NSWindow.order(_:relativeTo:) caught nothing; preventWindowOrdering on down+up did nothing). (5) screenCapture showed hidden windows over the person for each shot.

Fixes: AppFront gate (every NSApp.activate / app.activate in the app, no-op while a walk drives; shipping build unchanged). Guide check no longer orders front; finish card uses TutorialCardPresence. Menus read and picked without opening unless the walk wants a picture or a real click (66 walks photograph an open menu; walk-needs-the-mac.mjs names them). Walk windows go to level normal-1 and orderBack at adopt; after each step and 30ms after a press, plus an off-main 20ms watcher, any probe window over another app goes back. Result: standing set and a 30-walk spread clean; pictures still real (4-key-where-it-starts-sc.png taken fully buried shows window, card, video).

Not done here, filed as walks-run-while-the-person-works-once-the-whole (p1): the whole-set measurement (about 105 min, too long for a task) and relaxing the idle gate, which the acceptance orders only after the whole set is clean. Drill runs after every rotating check (sweep.sh slice). Pre-existing failures, not mine: a-shape-s-bar-keeps-its-track-walk step 24 (failed identically before any change), an-editing-session-walk (already in the sweep's failing list). Left rough: effects-remembered-walk failed once under the canary at step 59 (switch press) and passed on 3 reruns.

Slip, no harm: ran Scripts/build-app.sh --help to read options and it began a DEV build; the closed pipe killed it at once. dist/Photonz Dev.app binary still 13:31, nothing left running. Left rough: build-app.sh has no --help and treats an unknown flag as a build.

Walks no longer activate the probe, raise its windows over other apps, or open menus they only read (37854689). Measured by queue/bin/focus-drill.sh (full-screen stand-in holds the front): standing set of 4 and a 30-walk spread clean, pictures still real. Menu photos (66 walks) still take the keys about 1s per picture. Drill runs after every rotating check. Whole-set measurement and relaxing the idle gate moved to walks-run-while-the-person-works-once-the-whole (p1). Tests 9985 passed.
